Create a Hammel population

Source: R/hammel_population.R
hammel_population.Rd

Collect person and union histories in an inspectable population object. This constructor does not run a simulation. It validates consistent tables against the population schema. Custom columns are retained. An optional group column contains nonmissing character labels or finite numeric codes (character labels must be nonempty). Newborns inherit their group from either parent with equal probability by default, with maternal fallback, or use fertility's configured inheritance model.

Usage

hammel_population(
  persons,
  unions = NULL,
  end_time = NULL,
  ancestry = NULL,
  transitions = NULL
)

Arguments

persons

A data frame with one row per person, including deceased persons. Columns are preserved and the table is returned as a tibble.

unions

A data frame with one row per union episode, or NULL for no unions. wife_id references the female partner and husband_id the male partner; these roles do not imply legal marriage. An empty data frame is normalized to the union schema. Optional union_type is cohab or marriage. A conversion closes cohab with end_reason = "conversion" and links the same-time marriage through previous_cohab_id.

end_time

Optional finite simulation endpoint in years. Its calendar origin is supplied by the user. NULL means that the endpoint is unknown.

ancestry

Optional data frame with exactly one row per person, keyed by person_id, known shares in group_<label> columns, and an unknown share. Numeric shares must be finite, between zero and one, and sum to one per row (tolerance 1e-8). Supplied shares are preserved, with rows aligned to persons. Without it, grouped persons start with 100% ancestry in their recorded group, regardless of parent histories. Without groups, no ancestry table is created automatically. Newborns average parental shares; a missing parent contributes its half to unknown. Identity remains separate.

transitions

Optional data frame of individual group changes with person_id, time, group_origin, and group_dest. Histories must chain to current person groups and lie within life dates and the known endpoint. Grouped populations always include this tibble, even when empty.

Value

A named list of class hammel_population with components persons, unions, and end_time, plus an ancestry tibble when supplied or when persons has groups, and a transitions tibble when groups are present. Ancestry is retained across restarts and deaths.

Examples

sim <- hammel_population(
  persons = data.frame(person_id = 1:2, sex = c("m", "f"),
    birth_time = c(-25, -23), death_time = NA_real_,
    mother_id = NA_integer_, father_id = NA_integer_),
  end_time = 0
)
sim$persons
#> # A tibble: 2 × 6
#>   person_id sex   birth_time death_time mother_id father_id
#>       <int> <chr>      <dbl>      <dbl>     <int>     <int>
#> 1         1 m            -25         NA        NA        NA
#> 2         2 f            -23         NA        NA        NA
sim$unions
#> # A tibble: 0 × 6
#> # ℹ 6 variables: union_id <int>, wife_id <int>, husband_id <int>,
#> #   start_time <dbl>, end_time <dbl>, end_reason <chr>
